title: A Programming-Free Three-Dimensional Resonant Current-Mode Wireless Receiver with Real-Time Link-Adaptivity and a 0.904cm3 Receiver Coil for Implantable Systems
problem: Wireless power transfer (WPT) for implantable medical devices (IMDs) must balance high efficiency, small form factor, tissue safety (heating, EM field exposure), and surgical practicality while enabling wireless charging without infection risk.
motivation: Battery-based IMDs require surgical replacement and risk infection; wireless power eliminates these risks but demands compact receivers, efficient power extraction, and autonomous adaptation to body tissue variability.
method: A resonant current-mode (RCM) WPT receiver with real-time link-adaptivity uses a 3D receiver coil (0.904cm³) for compact integration, autonomous tuning to tissue impedance variations, and low-power capability without programming overhead.
key_novelty: Programming-free real-time link-adaptivity in RCM WPT with compact 3D coil integration for implantable systems.
contributions: Programming-free real-time link-adaptivity for RCM WPT
Reduced tissue heating vs prior approaches
limitations: Abstract-only analysis; power efficiency, charging time, tissue heating levels, and in-vivo performance not quantified.
primary_theme: Compact adaptive wireless power for implantable devices
